parsed.explanation: A trans visitor who is outed faces identity-based criminalisation: the May 2026 bill, passed and widely expected to receive assent, imposes up to 3 years for identifying as transgender, longer for advocacy, criminalises crossdressing, and creates a duty to report, alongside existing 'unnatural carnal knowledge' law carrying up to 3 years. The state has raided and closed LGBTQ premises through national security, groups operate secretly, mob justice is documented, and no anti-discrimination recourse or relief is shown. No documented visitor sweeps or enforcement of the 2026 bill exist yet and its application to short-term visitors is unresolved, keeping this above the 0.15-0.25 documented-arrest tiers, but extrapolating from the criminalising regime, hostile official framing around children/family, and absence of remedy places it below unremedied facility-exclusion cases.
